# PR #5008: Patch: a GIGA card's placement highlight lights all four zones it will take, not only its anchor

Closes #4995

Selecting a playable GIGA card in hand now draws one green rounded oblong over all four zones of each offered placement (SPEC §3.2 footprint), measured from the zones' boxes so it follows layout and the second seat's flipped board. Hover or keyboard focus isolates one block while the rest dim; while dragging, the drag reticle's pad spans the hovered anchor's whole 2×2. Anchors keep the click, focus and drop; the highlight takes no hits. Client only: anchors come from `Highlight.glow`, never from re-deciding legality.

What changed:
- [giga.ts](apps/web/src/game/giga.ts): `GigaAnchor`, `gigaFootprint`, `gigaFootprintTestids`, `anchorOfTestid` (parses only `zone-you-*`), `isGigaHandCard` (live `keywords` override first, printed face second, so hand-granted and printed GIGA both count).
- [LanePick.tsx](apps/web/src/game/LanePick.tsx): exported `Box`, added exported `measureBoxes`; `measure` reuses it, behavior identical.
- [GigaPlacement.tsx](apps/web/src/game/GigaPlacement.tsx) (new) + [gigaPlacement.css](apps/web/src/game/gigaPlacement.css) (new): per-anchor green (`--glow-ready`) oblongs, `pointer-events: none`, active/dim states, dim-while-dragging; no animation, so Reduce Motion holds by construction.
- [Board.tsx](apps/web/src/game/Board.tsx): mounts `<GigaPlacement>` in `.field` after the lanes.
- [DragLayer.tsx](apps/web/src/game/drag/DragLayer.tsx): `reticleFor(spot, footprint)` unions the footprint's boxes for GIGA hand-card drags (`gigaPadFor`); hero-gem and all other paths byte-identical.
- [gigaPlacement.test.tsx](apps/web/src/game/gigaPlacement.test.tsx) (new): the 7 acceptance tests (unit row p1+p2, backrow, hover/focus isolation, non-GIGA unchanged, click/no-hit-target, drag pad, printed GIGA).

How tested (commands I ran, what they printed):
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/gigaPlacement.test.tsx` — 7 passed.
- Same plus `giga.test.tsx`, `PromptLane.test.tsx`, `src/test/ux/glow.test.ts`, `src/test/ux/drag-layer.test.tsx` — 5 files, 112 passed.

- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` green (needs `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` on this machine; default heap OOMs at ~2GB — environmental, also true without my change).
- `pnpm exec eslint apps/web` green; `cargo fmt --check` green. No spec/ruling changes, so no `spec check` delta.

Decisions the issue didn't settle (with rejected alternatives):
- Oblongs measure during render and re-render on resize/scroll, instead of the plan's layout-effect `setBoxes`: the repo's React Compiler lint forbids sync setState in effects and new suppressions, and inline disables of `react-hooks/*` are banned. ```text
# #4995: Patch: a GIGA card's placement highlight lights all four zones it will take, not only its anchor
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

## What it does

When a GIGA card in hand is playable (selected, or dragged), the board lights only the **anchor** zones the engine offers: one zone each, the top-left cell of the 2×2 block the card will fill. The player can't see that the card takes four zones, or which four. The highlight should cover all four zones of each offered placement, the same way the lane pick (`LanePick.tsx`, #2757) draws one oblong over a lane's four zones.

### What the code does now

- A GIGA stands in its anchor (lane L of its row) and covers the other row's lane L and both rows' lane L+1 (§3, `spec/03-*.md`; R3546000, R3546004). Only anchors whose four zones are free are offered (`legalActions`).
- The zone glow is per zone: `highlightFor` (`apps/web/src/game/actions.ts`) puts each legal zone's testid in `Highlight.glow`, `Zone.tsx` stamps `data-glow="ready"`, and `highlights.css` paints it. So a GIGA play only lights the anchor zone.
- A hand card already says it is GIGA (`CardInstance.giga`, and the `GIGA` keyword in `apps/web/src/wire/catalog.ts`). The board side's footprint rule is in `apps/web/src/game/giga.ts` (`gigaCellOf`), and the anchor's card is drawn across the block in `board.css` (the R3546004 block): for your units and the enemy backrow the block grows toward the other row downward, for the other two upward, and always to lane L+1.
- `LanePick.tsx` already measures a box from a set of zones' `getBoundingClientRect()`s (`measure`) and draws one fixed-position oblong per lane in `lanePick.css`, re-measured when the layout changes and when the board flips for the second seat. Reuse that pattern (or factor its measure out) rather than write a second one.

### Suggested approach

- For each offered GIGA anchor, draw one rounded highlight over the four zones it would take (the anchor, the other row's same lane, and both rows' lane L+1), measured from those zones' boxes. Keep the green "ready" colour of a placement glow (`--glow-ready`), not LanePick's blue selection colour.
- Two offered anchors can overlap (anchors at L and L+1 share lane L+1). Don't stack two blocks over each other unreadably: e.g. light the union of the offered zones while idle, and show the exact 2×2 block of the anchor under the pointer, the keyboard focus or the drag.
- The anchor zone stays the one that takes the click, focus and drop, as now. The highlight takes no hit (`pointer-events: none`, as in `lanePick.css`).
- A non-GIGA card's placement glow doesn't change.
- Honour Reduce Motion as `lanePick.css` does if the highlight animates.
- Client only (CLAUDE.md rule 7): the four zones come from the offered anchor and the GIGA footprint, never from re-deciding legality in the client.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Selecting a playable GIGA unit in hand lights all four zones of each offered placement, not only the anchor; a web unit test (beside `apps/web/src/game/giga.test.tsx`) proves it for your unit row and for the backrow footprint, including the flipped board of the second seat.
- [ ] Dragging a GIGA card over an offered anchor shows that placement's whole 2×2 block; overlapping offers stay readable (the test covers two adjacent offered anchors).
- [ ] A non-GIGA card's placement highlight is unchanged (an existing or new test pins it).
- [ ] The anchor zone still takes the click and the drop; the highlight is not a hit target.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test` and `pnpm exec eslint apps/web` are green; any new number is a named constant (rule 9).

## Links

- Lane pick it mirrors: #2757 (`apps/web/src/game/LanePick.tsx`, `lanePick.css`)
- GIGA drawing: #3546, #3555, R3546004

## Done when

- [ ] Selecting a playable GIGA unit lights each offered placement's four zones (unit row and backrow footprints, p1 and p2 seats).
- [ ] Drag hover pads the anchor's whole 2×2; adjacent anchors dim to one readable block on hover/focus.
- [ ] Non-GIGA placement glow is byte-identical behavior (test 4 + existing glow tests green).
- [ ] Anchor keeps click/drop; highlight never a hit target (test 5).
- [ ] Typecheck, eslint, and the test files above are green; no new constant, no `actions.ts`/`model.ts` change.

## Risks

- `CardView.keywords` is override-only: checking only it would miss printed GIGA (Spectre); checking only the catalog would miss hand-granted GIGA (GIGA-ify, Big Time Recruits). `isGigaHandCard` checks live-first-then-printed for this reason.
- Same-lane anchors in both rows (Flexible GIGA) yield identical oblong boxes; hover/focus `data-active` still distinguishes them.
- `reticleFor` returning null when a footprint zone is missing cannot happen (all zones always mount), but the fallback preserves today's single-box behavior for every non-GIGA drag.
- Rejected alternative: one merged union box per idle board instead of per-anchor oblongs — non-rectangular when anchors span rows, harder to test, and per-anchor blocks already paint the union.

## Open questions

None. No person-only step: all files are bot-editable, no secret or dashboard setting is involved, and no ruling is needed.

# #4995: Patch: a GIGA card's placement highlight lights all four zones it will take, not only its anchor
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

## What it does

When a GIGA card in hand is playable (selected, or dragged), the board lights only the **anchor** zones the engine offers: one zone each, the top-left cell of the 2×2 block the card will fill. The player can't see that the card takes four zones, or which four. The highlight should cover all four zones of each offered placement, the same way the lane pick (`LanePick.tsx`, #2757) draws one oblong over a lane's four zones.

### What the code does now

- A GIGA stands in its anchor (lane L of its row) and covers the other row's lane L and both rows' lane L+1 (§3, `spec/03-*.md`; R3546000, R3546004). Only anchors whose four zones are free are offered (`legalActions`).
- The zone glow is per zone: `highlightFor` (`apps/web/src/game/actions.ts`) puts each legal zone's testid in `Highlight.glow`, `Zone.tsx` stamps `data-glow="ready"`, and `highlights.css` paints it. So a GIGA play only lights the anchor zone.
- A hand card already says it is GIGA (`CardInstance.giga`, and the `GIGA` keyword in `apps/web/src/wire/catalog.ts`). The board side's footprint rule is in `apps/web/src/game/giga.ts` (`gigaCellOf`), and the anchor's card is drawn across the block in `board.css` (the R3546004 block): for your units and the enemy backrow the block grows toward the other row downward, for the other two upward, and always to lane L+1.
- `LanePick.tsx` already measures a box from a set of zones' `getBoundingClientRect()`s (`measure`) and draws one fixed-position oblong per lane in `lanePick.css`, re-measured when the layout changes and when the board flips for the second seat. Reuse that pattern (or factor its measure out) rather than write a second one.

### Suggested approach

- For each offered GIGA anchor, draw one rounded highlight over the four zones it would take (the anchor, the other row's same lane, and both rows' lane L+1), measured from those zones' boxes. Keep the green "ready" colour of a placement glow (`--glow-ready`), not LanePick's blue selection colour.
- Two offered anchors can overlap (anchors at L and L+1 share lane L+1). Don't stack two blocks over each other unreadably: e.g. light the union of the offered zones while idle, and show the exact 2×2 block of the anchor under the pointer, the keyboard focus or the drag.
- The anchor zone stays the one that takes the click, focus and drop, as now. The highlight takes no hit (`pointer-events: none`, as in `lanePick.css`).
- A non-GIGA card's placement glow doesn't change.
- Honour Reduce Motion as `lanePick.css` does if the highlight animates.
- Client only (CLAUDE.md rule 7): the four zones come from the offered anchor and the GIGA footprint, never from re-deciding legality in the client.

- [ ] Selecting a playable GIGA unit in hand lights all four zones of each offered placement, not only the anchor; a web unit test (beside `apps/web/src/game/giga.test.tsx`) proves it for your unit row and for the backrow footprint, including the flipped board of the second seat.
- [ ] Dragging a GIGA card over an offered anchor shows that placement's whole 2×2 block; overlapping offers stay readable (the test covers two adjacent offered anchors).
